findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses String for status and separate bools (is_validated, is_sent) for lifecycle instead of an enum/typestate. Impossible states are constructible: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, status="sent" with is_sent=false, or any arbitrary status string.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream logic may branch on inconsistent flags (e.g. sees is_sent=true but sent_at_epoch_ms is None, causing incorrect audit trails or lost proof), and any arbitrary status string is accepted without domain validation.
findings.fix: Replace status String with a domain enum (e.g. enum LedgerStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }). Replace is_validated and is_sent bools with a single typestate enum. Remove is_sent field. Make all fields private.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive-obsessed lifecycle flag. Holzman Rust requires replacing bool lifecycle flags, status strings, and Option lifecycle fields with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: No compile-time guarantee that status values are from a known set. Typos, unexpected strings, or stale values silently pass through. Violates the rule that data should be valid by construction.
findings.fix: Define `pub enum LedgerStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }` and replace `status: String` with `status: LedgerStatus`.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are primitive lifecycle flags. Holzman Rust explicitly requires replacing bool lifecycle flags with enums or typestates.
findings.failure_mode: Two independent bools create 4 possible states but only 3-4 are valid domain states. Cross-field invariants (sent implies validated, sent_at_epoch_ms populated when sent) cannot be enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Merge into a single typestate enum: `enum LedgerStage { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Remove both bool fields.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is an Option lifecycle field that should be type-enforced. When the ledger is in a sent state, sent_at_epoch_ms must always be Some; when not sent, it must be None. An Option field cannot enforce this invariant.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(0) with status not being sent, or leave it None while is_sent=true. No type-level enforcement of the dependency between sent-state and timestamp.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the typestate enum variant: `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. The type system guarantees it is present iff the ledger is sent.

findings.problem: All fields of LedgerWorkflow are pub, allowing any caller to construct arbitrary illegal states directly via struct literal syntax.
findings.failure_mode: External modules can create a LedgerWorkflow with any combination of status, is_validated, and is_sent, bypassing all intended invariants without needing a constructor.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a constructor or builder that enforces invariants, and derive Accessors (pub getters) only for allowed observations.

findings.problem: mark_sent performs mutation (String::to_string allocation) in what should be the pure deterministic core. The function takes ownership and mutates status with a heap-allocated String clone.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every call. The function should be a pure domain transition returning a new typestate variant, not mutating a struct with String fields.
findings.fix: Rework mark_sent as a pure domain transition: `fn mark_sent(stage: LedgerStage) -> Result<LedgerStage, TransitionError>` that returns a `LedgerStage::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms }` variant. Move any clock/IO calls to the imperative shell.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LedgerWorkflow directly with no error type. A transition that requires preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent) has no way to express failure.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions are silently accepted or silently produce incorrect state. No caller can distinguish a successful transition from a no-op or ignored precondition.
findings.fix: Return `Result<LedgerStage, TransitionError>` where TransitionError is a typed domain error enum (e.g. `InvalidTransition { from: LedgerStage }`).

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for any performance claim. The code allocates String::to_string on every mark_sent call.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation cost in hot paths is unmeasured and unbounded. In high-throughput scenarios this causes unnecessary heap churn.
findings.fix: Add a micro-benchmark for mark_sent. Refactor to avoid String allocation by using the enum typestate pattern (zero-cost state transition).

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, allocation, or second-ring command evidence exists.
findings.failure_mode: Performance characteristics of the mark_sent path are unverified. Allocation patterns (String::to_string on every call) are unmeasured.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or simple time benchmark for mark_sent. Profile with `cargo +nightly bench` to confirm no unnecessary allocations.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance
no profiler data for allocation patterns
no allocation tracking evidence (e.g. dhat or AllocCounter)
no second-ring command evidence (no cargo test/clippy/bench output)
residual_risk: High. The entire LedgerWorkflow domain model is represented with primitive types (String, bool, Option) instead of type-enforced invariants. Illegal states are directly constructible and no error taxonomy exists for domain transitions. Static review only; no commands run. All lifecycle invariants depend on runtime discipline rather than compiler guarantees.
